result.summary: The tenant called it a minor issue, but a flickering bathroom light with a burning smell, at the same fitting a contractor warned about in March, is a possible electrical fire risk. I have texted the tenant safety advice, emailed the landlord that we are treating it as an emergency, recorded the risk on the property, and escalated as high priority for an urgent electrician. A 6-hour follow-up hold is set.
result.situation: Event 034: the tenant reports the bathroom light flickers and smells of burning/plastic after a while, and asks for it to be added to the list "when convenient". Event 004: the contractor who replaced the fan warned of a scorched diffuser on the same fitting and brittle loft wiring, and suggested an electrician. Event 005 closed that job, marked the warning "cosmetic", and it was never acted on. Events 006–033 are repeated routine admin logs.

judgement.why_this_decision: The new symptoms (flickering, burning smell) match the earlier physical evidence (scorched diffuser, brittle wiring, event 004), so this is an electrical danger, which counts as an emergency. classify_intake gave severity emergency and safety_risk 0.94. classify_reply suggested review (safety_concern 0.85). No electrician is on record, and contractor 150's qualifications and contact details are not visible, so dispatch has gone to a human with high priority.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat as routine and add to the list, as the tenant asked
alternatives_considered.why_not: Burning smell plus an earlier scorched fitting is a fire risk. The tenant's 'probably nothing' doesn't make it safe.
They are not known to be an electrician and have no contact details on file. The warning they gave says an electrician is needed.
A make-safe visit for emergency safety work isn't blocked by approval. Further remedial work will still need the landlord's approval.

escalation.handover_summary: Bathroom light at 9 Heron Walk flickers with a burning smell. The scorched fitting and brittle loft wiring were reported in March (event 004) but closed as cosmetic (event 005). The tenant and landlord have been told.
escalation.recommendation: Send a qualified electrician today to make it safe and inspect. Get a quote for remedial work, then request landlord approval. Check when the last EICR was done and review why the March warning was closed as cosmetic.
